N_PLUS_1.title: Possible N+1 query
N_PLUS_1.problem: Called very often and returns about one row each time. This usually means reads inside a loop, though statistics alone cannot prove it.
N_PLUS_1.fix: Combine the reads in the loop into one batched statement.
N_PLUS_1.app: Find the loop calling this statement, collect the ids and read them in one query. With an ORM, eager load the association.

POLLING.title: Frequent polling
POLLING.problem: The statement runs many times per minute and takes a share of total load.
POLLING.fix: Poll less often, cache the result, or use LISTEN/NOTIFY.
POLLING.app: Find the timer or worker loop; trigger on change instead, or cache the result briefly.

MISSING_INDEX.title: Missing index
MISSING_INDEX.problem: A large table is scanned end to end, while the filter selects only a small part of it.
MISSING_INDEX.fix: Create the index below at a quiet time. Account for the extra write cost and disk space.
MISSING_INDEX.app: Add the index with a migration, not application code. CONCURRENTLY cannot run in a transaction, so run that migration outside one.

NON_SARGABLE.title: Function or cast on a column
NON_SARGABLE.problem: Applying a function to a column in WHERE stops its plain index from being used.
NON_SARGABLE.fix: Turn the condition into a range or create an expression index. Check time zones with date conversions.
NON_SARGABLE.app: Remove the function from the code building this statement: normalize the parameter first and compare the bare column.

LEADING_WILDCARD.title: LIKE with a leading wildcard
LEADING_WILDCARD.problem: A '%text' pattern cannot use a B-tree index, so the table is scanned.
LEADING_WILDCARD.fix: Create a GIN index with pg_trgm, or use full-text search.
LEADING_WILDCARD.app: Check whether the search really needs this pattern; switching to a prefix search may be enough.

LARGE_IN.title: Variable length IN list
LARGE_IN.problem: PostgreSQL treats each list length as a different statement, which fragments the plan cache and statistics.
LARGE_IN.fix: Use one array parameter with = ANY($1).
LARGE_IN.app: Bind the list as an array instead of individual parameters, so the statement text stays constant.

IMPLICIT_CAST.title: Parameter type does not match the column
IMPLICIT_CAST.problem: PostgreSQL has to convert the column, so its index cannot be used.
IMPLICIT_CAST.fix: Send the parameter with the column's type. Make sure the value converts to that type.
IMPLICIT_CAST.app: Fix the parameter type in your driver or ORM, for example do not send text for a numeric column.

OFFSET_PAGING.title: OFFSET pagination
OFFSET_PAGING.problem: OFFSET still reads every skipped row, so deep pages get slower.
OFFSET_PAGING.fix: Switch to keyset pagination. This affects API behaviour: jumping to a page number goes away.
OFFSET_PAGING.app: Return and accept the key of the last row as a cursor rather than a page number.

SELECT_STAR.title: SELECT *
SELECT_STAR.problem: Unneeded columns are read and sent over the network, and index-only scans are ruled out.
SELECT_STAR.fix: List only the columns you use. The suggested SQL lists them all; remove what is unused. The application must read columns by name.
SELECT_STAR.app: Work out which fields are really used; use a projection or DTO in your ORM.

TEMP_SPILL.title: Spilling to temp files
TEMP_SPILL.problem: A sort or hash does not fit in work_mem and writes to disk.
TEMP_SPILL.fix: Add an index that provides the order, or raise work_mem for this operation.
TEMP_SPILL.app: Do not raise work_mem globally. If needed, use SET LOCAL in this operation's transaction.

NO_LIMIT.title: Large result with no limit
NO_LIMIT.problem: Thousands of rows come back on each call and there is no LIMIT.
NO_LIMIT.fix: Add LIMIT or pagination if the application does not need every row.
NO_LIMIT.app: Move filtering from memory into SQL; use streaming or batches for bulk jobs.

RANDOM_SORT.title: ORDER BY random()
RANDOM_SORT.problem: It reads and sorts every row, which is very expensive on large tables.
RANDOM_SORT.fix: Use TABLESAMPLE or pick random ids. The distribution will not be identical.
RANDOM_SORT.app: Check whether the feature really needs a perfectly even distribution.

CORRELATED_SUBQUERY.title: Correlated subquery
CORRELATED_SUBQUERY.problem: The subquery may run again for each row of the outer query.
CORRELATED_SUBQUERY.fix: Consider rewriting with JOIN or LATERAL, and verify the results stay the same.
CORRELATED_SUBQUERY.app: Find the ORM association or property that computes this field and load it in bulk.

NOT_IN_SUBQUERY.title: NOT IN (subquery)
NOT_IN_SUBQUERY.problem: A NULL in the subquery makes it return no rows, and the planner optimizes it poorly.
NOT_IN_SUBQUERY.fix: Use NOT EXISTS. If the columns can be NULL the results change, so check first.
NOT_IN_SUBQUERY.app: Change the NOT IN condition in your query builder to NOT EXISTS.

COUNT_FOR_EXISTS.title: COUNT used as an existence check
COUNT_FOR_EXISTS.problem: Every match is counted just to see whether any row exists.
COUNT_FOR_EXISTS.app: Replace count() > 0 checks with your ORM's exists method.

OR_COLUMNS.title: OR across different columns
OR_COLUMNS.problem: An OR condition cannot be served by one index and can cause a table scan.
OR_COLUMNS.fix: If the plan shows a scan, consider splitting into two statements with UNION.
OR_COLUMNS.app: Consider separate statements in the code that builds dynamic filters.

CTE_MATERIALIZED.title: Materialized CTE
CTE_MATERIALIZED.problem: Outer filters cannot be pushed into a materialized CTE.
CTE_MATERIALIZED.fix: Try NOT MATERIALIZED if the CTE has no volatile functions or writes.
CTE_MATERIALIZED.app: Update the CTE where the statement is built and compare the plans.

HIGH_VARIANCE.title: Highly variable duration
HIGH_VARIANCE.problem: Some calls are far above the mean; this may be value skew or plan changes.
HIGH_VARIANCE.fix: In the Plan tab, take a custom plan with values you know are slow.
HIGH_VARIANCE.app: Find which parameters the slow calls use from application logs or auto_explain.

LOW_CACHE.title: Low cache hit ratio
LOW_CACHE.problem: The statement reads a lot of its data from disk.
LOW_CACHE.fix: Reduce the data scanned with an index; review shared_buffers if needed.
LOW_CACHE.app: Check whether the date range or row count this statement reads can be narrowed.

WAL_HEAVY.title: Heavy WAL generation
WAL_HEAVY.problem: Each call generates a lot of WAL, which puts pressure on replication and disk.
WAL_HEAVY.fix: Split large writes into smaller pieces; reduce unneeded indexes and column updates.
WAL_HEAVY.app: Split bulk updates into batches and leave unchanged columns out of the UPDATE.

JIT_OVERHEAD.title: High JIT overhead
JIT_OVERHEAD.problem: A significant part of the time goes to JIT compilation.
JIT_OVERHEAD.fix: Consider raising jit_above_cost or disabling JIT for this statement.
JIT_OVERHEAD.app: If needed, use SET LOCAL jit = off before this statement.

PLAN_HEAVY.title: High planning time
PLAN_HEAVY.problem: A significant part of the time goes to planning.
PLAN_HEAVY.fix: Use prepared statements; review the partition and join counts.
PLAN_HEAVY.app: Enable prepared statements in your driver; with PgBouncer check that the pool mode supports them.
